```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# The clean data. This solution lives in exercises/facilitator/, next to the
# exercise folder.
hh <- read.csv(file.path("..", "explore_exercise", "household_water_clean.csv"))

# STEP 5: remove the # and fill the ___ (the variable for "interviewed in the
# last 7 days of fieldwork")
if (params$last_week_only) hh <- filter(hh, last_week == 1)
```

## Summary

<!-- STEP 4: replace ___ below (keep the quotes) with the variable for
     "chlorinated on 1+ of the past 7 days". The household count is already
     done for you. -->

This report covers **`r format(nrow(hh), big.mark = ",")` households**. **`r round(100 * mean(hh[["chlorine_any"]], na.rm = TRUE), 1)`%** of them added chlorine to their drinking water on at least one day in the past week.

## Descriptives by water source

```{r descriptives, eval = TRUE}
# STEP 2: replace each ___ with a variable name, then set eval = TRUE above
hh %>%
  group_by(piped) %>%                                      # water source: piped or not
  summarise(N               = n(),
            chlorinated_pct = 100 * mean(chlorine_any, na.rm = TRUE),  # chlorinated, 1+ of past 7 days
            chlorine_days   = mean(chlorine_days, na.rm = TRUE),        # days chlorinated
            boiled_pct      = 100 * mean(boil_any, na.rm = TRUE),  # boiled, 1+ of past 7 days
            stored_pct      = 100 * mean(stored_now, na.rm = TRUE),  # has water stored now
            very_safe_pct   = 100 * mean(safe_very, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%  # rates water very safe
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

## Main outcome

```{r figure, eval = TRUE, fig.height = 3.5}
# STEP 3: replace each ___ with a variable name, then set eval = TRUE above
hh %>%
  group_by(village_id) %>%                                       # village
  summarise(chlorinated_pct = 100 * mean(chlorine_any, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%  # chlorinated, 1+ of past 7 days
  ggplot(aes(factor(village_id), chlorinated_pct)) +             # village again
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "Village", y = "Chlorinated, past 7 days (%)")
```
